intro.title: usePrevious
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom hook called usePrevious in Angular to track and display the previous value of a state variable. You will learn the core concept of using a ref to persist a value across component re-renders without triggering updates. The main technologies involved are Angular's framework with TypeScript, using signals for state management and the effect function for side effects. By the end, you will understand how to capture a value before it changes and apply this pattern in your own projects.
intro.usecase: The usePrevious pattern is essential in Angular applications where you need to track value changes over time. In dashboard components, it helps detect when a metric's value crosses a threshold to trigger visual alerts or notifications. Form validation benefits from comparing current and previous field values to show meaningful change-based error messages. Interactive data tables use it to preserve previous filter states, enabling undo functionality or showing what data changed after filtering.
